q: The Jewett-Krieger-Weiss theorem refines Jewett-Krieger: every aperiodic ergodic measure-preserving system is measurably isomorphic to a strictly ergodic (uniquely ergodic minimal) topological system. Moreover, the topological system can be chosen to be:
opts: A subshift (closed shift-invariant subset of A^ℤ for a finite alphabet A)
A rotation on a compact group
A minimal homeomorphism of the Cantor set only
exp: Weiss's theorem: every aperiodic ergodic MPT is isomorphic to a strictly ergodic subshift. The topological model is a subshift on a finite alphabet, with the unique invariant measure being the given measure. This gives measure-theoretic ergodic theory a natural symbolic topological model.
